title: Mesosurge Harmonics — calibration & quick log
content:
Goal:
Calibrate and characterize a mesosurge-shaped arrival pattern and its harmonic subbursts against the staging inference pool. Objective is to find the onset threshold where p99 jumps and to inspect whether prefix/KV cache coherence or worker eviction correlates with latency spikes.

High-level idea (mesosurge / harmonics):
- Drive load with a base sinusoidal QPS envelope (period 120s, amplitude 0.6*base) and overlay a faster harmonic (period 6s) that creates short microbursts inside the long wave. This mimics diurnal + microburst mixing we see in customer traffic (edge + background).
- Vary KV cache priming state (cold/partially-warm/warm) and two batching configs (aggressive timeout 2ms, conservative 15ms).

Environment / hardware:
- staging-dedicated-pool-4xA100-80GB (NVIDIA NVLink) — 4 GPU nodes, 16 workers total, server runtime v3.8.1
- model: redwood-v1-7b-quant (int8 friendly)
- runtime flags: continuous-batch=true, kv-cache=true (local per-worker), prefetch=on

Traffic generator (notes):
- generator: custom loadbench harness (go) that can emit amplitude-modulated sine + harmonic overlay.
- baseline QPS: 120 req/s (user-simulator), base payload ~40 tokens in / 80 tokens out average.
- harmonic overlay amplitude: +/- 40 req/s on a 6s period
- envelope period: 120s, amplitude +/- 70 req/s
- run length: 45 minutes per config (warmup 5m; measurement 40m)
- concurrency: client side unlimited (we rely on server backpressure to shape)

Test matrix (3 variables):
1) KV cache state: cold (restart workers before run), partial (30% prefix primed), warm (run with priming traffic 10m).
2) Batch timeout: 2ms (low latency) vs 15ms (higher batch).
3) Admission policy: default vs preemption-disabled (to see eviction behaviour).
Total runs: 3 * 2 * 2 = 12 runs.

Key metrics collected (per-second and per-request):
- p50/p90/p95/p99 latency (in ms) server-side and client-observed
- tail latency heatmap with burst alignment (time since nearest harmonic peak)
- throughput (completed tokens/sec, requests/sec)
- KV cache hit rate (per-prefix and aggregate)
- worker eviction/restart events, OOM warnings
- batch size distribution and batching delays (ms)

Commands / snippets used:
- start load: ./loadbench --pattern "meso:period=120:amp=70:harm:period=6:amp=40" --qps 120 --duration 2700
- capture hist: curl http://staging-metrics/api/hist?job=meso-harmonics
- query logs: gh pr link above has the small agent that annotates logs when harmonic peaks occur

Representative run notes (one config): KV=warm, timeout=2ms, preemptions=on
- warmup (0-5m): p50~9ms, p95~28ms, p99~52ms. KV-hit ~92% steadily. batches mostly size 1-2.
- measurement window (5-45m): average throughput ~118 rps, token/sec ~9400. Observed regularly recurring p99 spikes aligned to harmonic peaks (every ~6s). During microburst peaks p99 jumps to 220-300ms for short windows (200-500ms).
- heatmap shows two distinct modes: microburst aligned short tails (~250ms) and envelope-crest tails (~450-700ms) when harmonic peak aligns with envelope crest.
- stack traces show increased scheduling delay (worker busy loop), not memory pressure. No evictions.

Representative run notes (KV=cold, timeout=2ms):
- warmup effectively doesn't exist. Cold cache causes prefix fetch penalty: initial p99s in first 8m up to 1.2s. After priming, baseline tail drops but harmonic spikes are amplified (~400-800ms).
- KV-hit starts ~12% rising to 70% after 10m. During microburst peaks, hit rate dips briefly (local cache thrash).

Representative run notes (KV=partial, timeout=15ms):
- batching absorbs many of the microbursts; p50 increases slightly (by ~6ms) but p95/p99 are significantly lower during harmonic peaks (p99 median ~120ms, peak ~260ms).
- however when envelope crest and harmonic align, we still saw >600ms tails and transient worker thread scheduling backpressure.

Observations / hypotheses:
1) Harmonic microbursts are short enough that short batch timeouts (2ms) avoid adding large batching latency but expose scheduling contention — many single-token micro-requests fight for GPU kernel launch and context.
2) Longer batch timeouts (15ms) reduce p99 at the cost of higher p50. They are effective when microburst amplitude is high relative to baseline QPS.
3) Cold KV cache amplifies harmonic tails because misses trigger synchronous prefix loads that block the worker for >200ms. Local cache thrash observed when microburst spikes repeatedly target similar prefixes on same worker.
4) Evictions were not common in these runs; the tail appears more scheduling and batch-assembly related than OOM-driven.
5) Worst-case tails occur when harmonic peaks align with envelope crest — that multiplicative superposition drives per-worker scheduling to saturation.

Quick actionable experiments to follow (short list):
- Add a per-prefix staggered backoff: if a worker sees N misses for the same prefix in T sec, reply with soft-429 to client router so request can be routed to another worker that may have the prefix cached. (Prototype ticket JIRA-OPS-1056)
- Experiment with adaptive batch-timeout that drops to 1ms when transient queue depth < x, and increases to 20ms when harmonic detection sees rising QPS.
- Add microburst detector on the edge router that applies short-lived request shapers (token bucket smoothing for <200ms) only when harmonic amplitude crosses threshold.
- Instrument per-batch scheduling delay more precisely (time from deque to kernel launch) and correlate with microburst alignment.

Open questions / unknowns:
- Are kernels suffering from multi-tenant NVLink contention at harmonic peaks (need to repro with isolated single-worker runs)?
- Can we preempt some low-importance inflight batches safely to prioritize latency-sensitive small requests?
- How much of the effect depends on model quantization path (int8 vs fp16)? Plan to repeat 2 runs with fp16 variant.

Short-term actions (owner: Ashwin):
- Implement finer-grain scheduling histogram (due 2024-07-08) and re-run KV=warm, timeout=2ms case.
- File JIRA for per-prefix soft-429 elastic retry (ops + routing) and ping Mira for router changes.
- Draft a short note for SRE on observed correlation with harmonic alignment and ask for assistance on isolating NVLink/PCIe metrics.

Notes to self:
- save raw traces in s3://bench-raw/meso-harmonics/<run-id> and tag with harmonic-phase map (script attached in PR).
- this doc is deliberately rough — will extract a 1-page summary for product and CS after verifying fp16 runs.

End of runbook.
